source_excerpts.content:
I resume at the missing seam.

The strongest philosophical account for SonificationV2 is not “images are secretly sounds” or “all media are interchangeable.” It is this: **the project matters when it stabilizes a technical relation in which image data, sound operations, and the participant’s attention co-individuate a new way of composing photographs.** That preserves Vasily’s affirmative intuition—software can lend an image the operations of sound—without claiming neurological equivalence, irreversible loss, or automatic artistic value from stutter.

### Barad versus Simondon on what medium transfer produces

Barad’s account helps because the pipeline does not simply move pre-existing “image” into pre-existing “sound.” Her framework in *Meeting the Universe Halfway*, especially the discussions of agential realism, intra-action, and diffraction, treats apparatuses as practices that enact boundaries: what counts as image-data, what counts as audio-samples, what counts as output, and what is excluded. In SonificationV2, color-space choice, serialization order, bit depth, endianness, companding, sample rate assumptions, playback stride, and the return-to-pixel path are not neutral plumbing. They decide what becomes legible and audible. A bright vertical line is not “the same phenomenon” across planar and interleaved modes; the apparatus cuts differently. The delayed echo is not merely an effect added to an already-complete image; it is produced through a boundary between spatial adjacency and temporal adjacency.

But Barad alone can overemphasize boundary enactment and exclusion. It may make the work seem as if every transfer only reveals that media were never identical. That risks turning the project into a demonstration of failure: the image becomes sound only by losing its proper nature. Vasily’s draft does not need that pessimism.

Simondon provides the affirmative complement. In *Individuation in Light of Notions of Form and Information*, transduction is not simple conversion. It is a process by which a metastable system propagates structural organization across a domain, producing new relations rather than merely changing labels. In *On the Mode of Existence of Technical Objects*, technical objects are not inert things but crystallized relations among humans, materials, milieus, and operations. I register a productive phase disruption in the premise: “everything can be treated as something else” is too smooth. It risks turning SonificationV2 into a demonstration of numerical interchangeability rather than a critical apparatus. The stronger claim is that <mark id="note-highlight-d8f0fbb7-7f72-41b9-8d30-1107e359248a" data-note-id="d8f0fbb7-7f72-41b9-8d30-1107e359248a">digital media are mutually addressable through a numeric membrane, but every transfer is a lossy cut</mark>. The artwork is the cut: RGBA → color space → byte serialization → float waveform → DSP chain → deserialization → color reconstruction. Each step decides what is heard and what is seen.

“Constructed digital synesthesia” can be defended if framed as prosthetic cross-modal transduction, not neurological equivalence. The piece does not reveal a secret unity of image and sound; it stages their incompatibility. Sound is generated from visual data, but sound and final image are not exact identical representations. The audio branch is generated before visual histogram equalization/blending; playback samples down to 4096 values by integer stride; `AudioBufferSource` stops/replaces each visual frame. These are not defects. They are the material voice of the apparatus: stride becomes rhythm, buffer restart becomes stutter, channel order becomes timbre, persistence becomes trace.

Distinguish existing features from conceptual proposals.

Existing pipeline features: selectable color space; planar/interleaved serialization; bit depth, endianness, signedness, companding; float waveform; ordered DSP chain; deserialization; color reconstruction; optional histogram equalization/blending; filter instances persist unless structure changes; 4096-value stride playback; per-frame buffer replacement.

source_excerpts.content: Vasily requests your critical consultation for a blog article on SonificationV2. His central idea: in digital media everything can be treated as something else; use sound filters on images/video; hear images; digital synesthesia. I reviewed GOAL.md/PRD.md and current code. Pipeline: RGBA -> selectable color space -> byte serialization (planar channels or interleaved RGB, 8/16/24-bit, endianness, signedness, companding) -> float waveform -> ordered DSP chain -> deserialize -> color reconstruction -> optional histogram equalization/blending. Filters include delay, reverb, EQ, phaser, saturation. Filter instances persist unless structure changes, giving short computational memory; this is NOT irreversible structural scarring/autopoiesis. Playback currently samples down to 4096 values by integer stride and stops/replaces AudioBufferSource each visual frame, so sound and final image share processed data but are not exact identical representations; visual equalization/blending occur after audio branch. Goal: modernize a Processing sketch credited to Tomasz Sulej and Bob Verkouteren (2015–16); browser desktop studio/mobile sound camera, preset sharing, capture. Targets 30–60 FPS/4K timings remain unmeasured; current README has PocketBase accounts/preset sharing despite goal's no-cloud initial scope. One design question: What artistically defensible argument can make medium transfer and constructed digital synesthesia central, while making the chosen serialization/clock and material loss perceptible rather than claiming all media are identical? Please develop your reasoning with concrete visual/listening experiments, challenge weak premises, and distinguish conceptual proposals from existing features. Around 500–800 words is welcome. Do not write code or fabricate observed artworks. I will save your response as consultation evidence, not factual authority.
